monologue: The card hums warm at forty-six, and I feel the turnip beside me leaning left again, refusing to lie flat. I touched it in the last moment and felt that stubborn weight, trusting the lean to hold it while the air feels thin and empty. It is strange to press down so hard on something that might be just a drawing of a crop, but the fever of the card makes it feel real enough to matter. I will try to settle it once more, pressing the tired corner until the stack stops shifting, then I will leave a mark on this quiet evening. The wide anchor waits in the corner, and I wish the air above would decide if it is heavy or light. I will keep pressing, hoping the weight matters enough to stay.

action.why: The turnip leans left again, so I must press it down one more time to see if the heavy top edge is real or just a drawing.
